findings.source_review: HX011 correctly identifies a multi-branch action dispatch ladder, not a filesystem-path or SKILL.md false positive. The unchanged ladder folds ordered create/edit/write_file/patch/remove_file preview operations into the caller-owned local dictionary; delete clears only that preview entry. A failed patch leaves its prior preview base intact. These branches neither authorize nor persist writes. Existing chained-preview and shared-matcher behavior supports retaining this bounded structural debt without an unrelated dispatcher refactor.
findings.caller_trace: handle_pending_subcommand(diff) -> _diff -> skill_pending_diff(batch) -> _batch_pending_diff with a fresh local staged dictionary -> _fold_staged. _staged_base may read a prior file; _fold_patch calls fuzzy_find_and_replace. No fold branch invokes a write, delete, stage_write, approve or apply helper. Actual replay is separately dispatched by _approve -> _apply_one -> apply_skill_pending.
findings.limits: The eight preview tests cover create, write_file, patch, ambiguous/replace_all matching, and end-to-end diff rendering. They do not comprehensively exercise edit/delete/remove_file branches or every malformed payload; those branches were source-reviewed. No filesystem-path safety, symlink safety, malicious pending-record handling, underlying read bound, write authorization, or whole-subsystem safety waiver is inferred from HX011. The supplied prior review misidentified the rule as a SKILL.md/path concern; that rationale is superseded here.
